title: The sharper upscaler made the walls boil
claim: On AI-rendered anime video, a light temporal denoise followed by Real-ESRGAN animevideov3 x4 cuts background jitter by 51–58 % against NVIDIA RTX Video Super Resolution 4x and gives sharper faces, at the same ~4.8 minutes per episode.

headline.label: background jitter vs RTX VSR 4x ULTRA

summary: Four days after adopting RTX Video Super Resolution because it sharpened line art 1.9–2.7x over Lanczos, the background of every episode visibly boiled. A second benchmark added a flow-compensated jitter ruler and tested eight upscaler chains on three 124-frame takes (close, medium, wide) at 768² → 3072². RTX VSR doubled the source's background jitter (1.85–2.05x Lanczos) because it sharpens the renderer's frame-to-frame grain. A temporal hqdn3d prefilter followed by realesr-animevideov3 x4 was the steadiest arm (9–15 % below the plain Lanczos source) and the crispest on faces within the ten-minute budget. The studio switched its master upscale the same day. A sharpness metric alone picked the wrong upscaler.
limitations: Three takes from one look (gothic anime, 768² renders from one video model). Other styles and photoreal footage were not tested.
The jitter and shimmer rulers are the studio's own (flow-compensated residual on a background mask). They have not been validated against human ratings; there was no blind preference test.
The halo ruler penalises the winner's darker ink lines. The claim that this is not ringing rests on one person's inspection at 100 % zoom.
The winning chain flattens fine plaster mottling into painted flats; that loss is visible and is a taste trade-off, not a free win.
One GPU; both fast arms are bound by the x264 encode, so the timing parity may not hold on other hardware or encoders.

changelog.note: First publication, written up from the studio's 2026-10-14 and 2026-10-18 bench reports.
